# Limitations of Mtek v0.1

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/limitations.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale or disagrees with the diagnostics catalogue or with `mtek context` (decisions 0101 and 0103).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).

## 1. What this page is

The release contract of v0.1 is what the specification promises **and** a test proves. Everything on this page is excluded from that contract: it is rejected on purpose, it is specified but not built, or it is a measured weakness. Nothing here is hidden behind a softer word, and nothing on this page works "almost".

- Section 2 lists every `x9xx` diagnostic: the features that v0.1 refuses by name.
- Section 3 lists what this compiler build rejects with `E9010` although the specification describes it.
- Section 4 lists the reserved words.
- Section 5 lists the diagnostics that are in the catalogue but that no program of v0.1 can produce.
- Section 6 lists the documented restrictions of the specification and of decisions 0015 and 0016, by area.
- Section 7 is the list `mtek context` gives to AI agents, verbatim.

The reasons and the restrictions of sections 2, 3 and 6 are written by hand in `tools/release-docs/data/limitations.json`; each is anchored to a quotation of the specification that a test looks for, so a reason cannot outlive the sentence it rests on. Where the specification gives no reason beyond "not in v0.1", the entry says so.

`spec/diagnostics.md` section 3: within each range of codes, the `x9xx` codes mean "specified as not supported in v0.1". They are different from `E9010` (section 3 of this page) on purpose: a limit of the language is not a gap of the build.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `E5901` | scene switching not supported | Reserved: retired by decision 0141: `go_to(Scene)` switches the active scene, so no program produces it; the code is kept so that the number is not reused | Retired: `go_to(Scene)` switches the active scene (decision 0141), so no program produces this code. | `E5902` | transparency not supported | Reserved: retired by decision 0138: materials are translucent when a colour param has an alpha below 1, so no program produces it; the code is kept so that the number is not reused | Retired: a material colour param with an alpha below 1 makes the draw translucent (decision 0138), so no program produces this code. | `E7901` | remote assets not supported | an `http:`, `https:` or other URL as an asset path | Assets are compile-time dependencies that the compiler opens and validates while it checks the program (decision 0015); v0.1 offers no option to load remote assets. | [tests/assets/fail/e7901_remote_asset](../tests/assets/fail/e7901_remote_asset) |

## 3. Gates of this build: specified, not implemented

`E9010` means "specified for v0.1 but not implemented by this compiler build yet". These are the gates the build has; `mtek context` lists each under `notSupported`.

### `non-constant-initial-values`

- Diagnostic: `E9010`.
- What is rejected: The initial value of an entity or camera field, of a material instance parameter or of a projection field that is not a constant expression is rejected (for example `position: vec3(half(1.0), 0.0, 0.0)`, which calls a user function). A scene `state` initialiser is not affected by this gate (a `state` initialised by a pure user function checks and builds).
- Why: Specified for v0.1 but not implemented: spec/scenes.md section 11 evaluates such values once at construction, but this build folds every initial value at compile time, so it stops at the first value it cannot fold instead of approximating it. No milestone is planned for it (decision 0086 item 2).
- Records: [0039](../spec/decisions/0039-materials-in-the-checker-details.md), [0086](../spec/decisions/0086-diagnostic-wording-and-baseline-frame-order.md), [0094](../spec/decisions/0094-coverage-audit-findings.md).
- Source: [spec/decisions/0086-diagnostic-wording-and-baseline-frame-order.md](../spec/decisions/0086-diagnostic-wording-and-baseline-frame-order.md): "the build still folds every initial value"

## 4. Reserved words (27)

The words are reserved for future use (spec/language.md 2.3); using one as a name is E0013 ("`while` is reserved for a future version"). The specification gives no further rationale. ([spec/language.md](../spec/language.md): "Using these as identifiers is error `E0013`")

`as` `async` `await` `extern` `impl` `loop` `mod` `move` `mut` `priv` `pub` `static` `super` `trait` `type` `unsafe` `use` `where` `yield` `compute` `vertex` `storage` `uniform` `workgroup` `system` `query` `component`

## 5. Specified, but no program can produce the diagnostic (4)

These codes are in the catalogue and are marked there. Each stays in the catalogue so that the number is not reused; none has a negative test, because no program of v0.1 can reach it. `tests/semantics/code-coverage-exceptions.json` holds the reasons, and a test fails when one of these codes gains a fixture without leaving the list.

| Code | Title | Mark in the catalogue | Why no program produces it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `E5100` | non-opaque color in material parameter | Reserved | Retired by decision 0138: material colour params take any alpha (an alpha below 1 makes the draw translucent), so no program can produce it; the catalogue keeps the code so that the number is not reused. |
| `E5901` | scene switching not supported | Reserved | Retired by decision 0141: go_to(Scene) switches the active scene, so no program can produce it; the catalogue keeps the code so that the number is not reused. |
| `E5902` | transparency not supported | Reserved | Retired by decision 0138: a material colour param with an alpha below 1 makes the draw translucent, so no program can produce it; the catalogue keeps the code so that the number is not reused. |
| `W0030` | naming convention | Not implemented | The naming lint is not part of v0.1 (spec/language.md section 3.3 as amended by decision 0102; decision 0070 item 11): neither the compiler nor mtek fmt implements it, the catalogue keeps the code so that the number is not reused, and no program can produce it. |

`W0030` is the one that the language reference used to promise: the formatter's naming lint. `spec/language.md` section 3.3 now says that the lint is not part of v0.1, and the catalogue keeps the code (decisions 0070 item 11 and 0102). The naming conventions of that section are conventions only; nothing checks them.

| Continuous collision is opt-in: `Dynamic { continuous: true }` for one body, or the host option `physics.continuousCollision` for every dynamic body. With it off, a small body can tunnel through a thin moving obstacle: the recorded radius-0.05 m ball and 0.1 m moving plate tunnel above 7.2 m/s at 60 Hz, depending on phase. With it on, no lane tunnels inside the published envelope: shots of 0.05 m or more at 3 to 240 m/s against static walls, kinematic walls moving at most 1 m/s toward the shot and dynamic plates at rest or moving at most 1 m/s toward it (6 480 matrix lanes, and lanes D00 to D16 of `physics_tunnel`). Outside it, obstacles that move faster on their own, shots above 250 m/s at a moving obstacle and everything not measured (other fixed steps, smaller, oblique or spinning shots, two fast bodies meeting) can still tunnel, and a teleport is never swept (decisions 0193 and 0216). | The default retains the recorded discrete-physics contract; continuous collision adds solver work and, for a continuous body, a 0.2 mm contact skin and a 0.1 mm allowed linear error.
